# TermPop

> TermPop is a browser extension for reading technical content. It highlights terms and offers contextual explanations without making the reader leave the current page.

## Official links

- Website: https://termpop.com/
- Quick-start guide: https://termpop.com/guide?lang=en
- Documentation: https://termpop.com/docs?lang=en
- Source code and releases: https://github.com/fangbm/TermPop
- Microsoft Edge Add-ons: https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/termpop/blphbffphknkkblackimhnjbckegnchn

## Capabilities

- Highlights technical terms in ordinary web pages.
- Explains a hovered term or a user-selected phrase in context.
- Supports hover, selection, and hybrid reading modes.
- Supports screenshot explanations with a vision-capable model or local OCR fallback.
- Includes a dedicated PDF viewer; direct injection into built-in browser PDF viewers is not supported.
- Uses a Rust and WebAssembly core for local term matching.
- Provides a personal dictionary, ignored-term list, and separate term and explanation caches.

## Privacy and LLM configuration

- Core Rust/WebAssembly matching runs locally in the browser.
- Users can configure a bring-your-own-key provider locally.
- When an LLM feature is used, only the needed selected text, contextual excerpt, or enabled screenshot is sent to that user-selected provider.
- API keys are stored in browser local storage and are not hardened secret storage.

## Browser support

- Microsoft Edge and Chromium-based browsers.
- The Edge store is the preferred download destination for Microsoft Edge.
